s: Chapter I: application, definitions, general explanations
अध्याय 1: लागू होना, परिभाषाएँ, साधारण स्पष्टीकरण
en:
Chapter I on one page

1Name, start date, and where the Sanhita applies
239 definitions, now in one alphabetical section
3Nine reading rules, including common intention
Section 1

Short title, commencement and application

Sub-s.RuleIPC
(1)Called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 20231
(2)In force from the notified date: 1 July 2024—
(3)Every person, for acts within India2
(4)Offence beyond India, triable here by law: dealt with as if done in India3
(5)Reaches three situations outside India4
(6)Mutiny and desertion Acts, special and local laws untouched5
  • S.1(5): (a) a citizen of India anywhere · (b) any person on a ship or aircraft registered in India · (c) any person abroad targeting a computer resource located in India
  • Notification S.O. 850(E) of 23 February 2024 left out s.106(2)
Section 2

Definitions

Cl.Term and meaningIPC
(3)Child: any person below 18 yearsnew
(7)Dishonestly: intention of wrongful gain to one or wrongful loss to another24
(8)Document: now includes electronic and digital record29
(9)Fraudulently: with intention to defraud, not otherwise25
(10)Gender: “he” covers male, female or transgender8
(11)Good faith: nothing done without due care and attention52
(14)Injury: harm illegally caused in body, mind, reputation or property44
(21)Movable property: every description, except land and things attached to the earth22
(28)Public servant: eleven descriptions, (a) to (k)21
(33)Voluntarily: intended it, or knew or had reason to believe it likely39
  • Old Code spread these over ss.8–52A; the Sanhita puts them in one section, alphabetically
  • Cl.(39): terms not defined here take their meaning from the IT Act, 2000 and the BNSS
Dr. Vimla v. Delhi Administration1963verify“Defraud” needs deceit plus injury to the person deceived
Dishonestly · s.2(7)Fraudulently · s.2(9)
Wrongful gain or loss of propertyIntention to defraud
Deception not requiredDeception is the core
Always about propertyInjury need not be to property
Section 3

General explanations

Sub-s.Reading ruleIPC
(1)Every offence is read subject to the General Exceptions6
(2)An expression once explained keeps that sense throughout7
(3)Held by spouse, clerk or servant on your account = your possession27
(4)Words about acts extend to illegal omissions32
(5)Common intention: each liable as if he did it alone34
(6)Act criminal only by knowledge or intention: liable to the extent of his own35
(7)Effect caused partly by act, partly by omission: same offence36
(8)Intentionally doing one of several acts = committing the offence37
(9)Same criminal act, different offences for different persons38
  • S.3(5) needs three things: a criminal act by several persons · a common intention of all · the act done in furtherance of it
  • S.3(3): the old Code said “wife”; the Sanhita says “spouse”

You did not strike the blow. You shared the intention. You answer for the act.

Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. King Emperor1925verifyStanding guard as part of the plan is participation
Mahbub Shah v. Emperor1945verifySame or similar intention is not common intention; a pre-arranged plan is needed
Pandurang v. State of Hyderabad1955verifyPrior meeting of minds must be shown
Common intention · s.3(5)Common object · s.190
Old s.34 IPCOld s.149 IPC
Several persons (two or more)Unlawful assembly: five or more
Rule of joint liability, not an offence by itselfMakes every member guilty of the offence
Needs prior meeting of mindsMembership at the time is enough

Do not mix these up

“Child” in s.2(3) is under 18. The general exceptions for a child are under 7 (s.20) and 7 to 12 (s.21).

Movable property: the old s.22 said “corporeal property”. The Sanhita drops “corporeal”.

S.1(5)(c), the computer-resource limb, covers any person, not only citizens.

धारा 3

साधारण स्पष्टीकरण

उपधारापढ़ने का नियमभा.दं.सं.
(1)प्रत्येक अपराध साधारण अपवादों के अधीन पढ़ा जाएगा6
(2)एक बार स्पष्ट किया गया पद सर्वत्र उसी अर्थ में7
(3)आपकी ओर से पति या पत्नी, लिपिक या सेवक के कब्जे में = आपका कब्जा27
(4)कार्यों के निर्देशक शब्द अवैध लोपों पर भी लागू32
(5)सामान्य आशय: प्रत्येक ऐसे दायी मानो उसी ने अकेले किया34
(6)कार्य केवल ज्ञान या आशय से आपराधिक: अपने ज्ञान या आशय तक दायी35
(7)परिणाम अंशतः कार्य, अंशतः लोप से: वही अपराध36
(8)कई कार्यों में से एक साशय करना = अपराध करना37
(9)एक ही आपराधिक कार्य, विभिन्न व्यक्तियों के लिए भिन्न अपराध38
  • धारा 3(5) के तीन तत्व: कई व्यक्तियों द्वारा आपराधिक कार्य · सबका सामान्य आशय · कार्य उसी को अग्रसर करने में किया गया
  • धारा 3(3): पुरानी संहिता में “पत्नी” था; नई संहिता में “पति या पत्नी”

वार आपने नहीं किया। आशय आपका भी था। कार्य का उत्तर आप भी देंगे।
